items.evidence: Two independent dead causes, all javap-verified fresh against the 1.21.11 jar. (1) Dead tag: speleothem_tag() reads #minecraft:speleothems (speleothem.rs:13), absent from 1.21.11 data (no tag file in the client jar, no BlockTags.SPELEOTHEMS field, no key in the prepared tag bundle), so speleothem_with / speleothem_is_tip / is_free_hanging_stalactite are always false and falling.rs:51 spawn_falling_stalactite is tag-gated; the thickness calc is tag-gated the same way (shapes.rs:1176 speleothem_thickness, place.rs:1398 speleothem_thickness_for, is_with closure at shapes.rs:1186), so thickness is always 'tip'. (2) Missing link: prepared fields for pointed_dripstone is {} (no blockToGrowOn), so data.link is None and speleothem_grow's can_grow is always false; vanilla 1.21.11 PDB.canGrow hardcodes Blocks.DRIPSTONE_BLOCK + water source at above(2). Vanilla PDB bytecode has ZERO BlockTags references - all predicates are same-block. Observable: transfer, growth, cauldron fill, thickness, falling stalactite spawn all dead. NOT dead (dispatch adapted IN THE TEMPLATE): all five dispatch sites arm on Class::Speleothem | Class::PointedDripstone (place.rs:1156, shapes.rs:745, survive.rs:326, tick.rs:257, tick.rs:443), so placement direction, updateShape scheduling, canSurvive, scheduled-tick destroy, fallOn damage and trident break all work. REPRODUCES 1.21.10 B1-G01 in the same narrower form; the 1.21.10 child inherited it from this template.
items.title: Pointed-dripstone system half dead: transfer, growth, cauldron fill, thickness, falling stalactites

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.11 FallingBlockEntity.tick (re-verified fresh): a falling concrete-powder entity computes inWater = block is ConcretePowderBlock && fluid at blockPosition is in the WATER tag, plus a COLLIDER + SOURCE_ONLY clip when the delta's length-squared is greater than 1.0; the landing branch runs when onGround() || inWater. The port's game/falling_blocks.rs fall_step has NO concrete-powder water check (landing only on on_ground; the comment at line 120 says 'a falling block never runs baseTick, so it is never in water'), and game/falling_damage.rs finish_falling_block calls falling_block_landed(..., false) - stuck_in_water=false always (line 128-133). So powder sinks to the lakebed and lands there as powder. The horizon-world landing branch itself (level/falling.rs falling_block_landed) matches vanilla, including the onLand solidify check (falling.rs:127) - the fix is local to the client fall step. REPRODUCES 1.21.10 B1-G02 and pilot G2.
items.title: Concrete powder falling into water does not solidify on contact

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.11 AbstractThrownPotion.onHitBlock gates on PotionContents.is(Potions.WATER) - Holder equality, NOT a tag (Potions.WATER getstatic at two gate sites, zero douses_fire / PotionTags references in the class, re-verified fresh). The port's game/splash_water.rs ships the 26.3 tag form (potion_in_tag for minecraft:douses_fire, minecraft:hurts_water_sensitive_entities, minecraft:extinguishes_entities, minecraft:rehydrates_axolotls), read from trades.potion_tags built from the prepared tags/potion directory - which is EMPTY for 1.21.11 (zero potion tag files in the client jar). All four gates are always closed: no splash water ever douses fire, hurts water-sensitive entities, extinguishes burning entities, or rehydrates axolotls. The downstream code matches vanilla exactly (dowse targets, dowseFire, the (4,2,4) box, dist2<16, hurt 1.0 indirectMagic, axolotl +1800 air capped - Axolotl.rehydrate re-verified fresh) but is unreachable. REPRODUCES 1.21.10 B1-G03 and B11-G13.
items.title: Splash water never douses fire / hurts / extinguishes / rehydrates

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.11 has the CLASSIC 1.21.x form - NO EntityFluidInteraction class at all (0 matches in either jar). Entity.updateFluidOnEyes is a single-cell check: top = eye-cell y + plain FluidState.getHeight, top > eyeY -> tags added. The port's horizon-world/src/entity_fluid.rs:389-401 computes the top with world.camera_height(state, p) (fluid.rs camera_height_at: a source fluid with a sturdy block above -> 1.0, else height_at) instead of the plain top. Observable: an entity whose eye is in (0.889, 1.0] above a source's block bottom with a solid ceiling -> the port says eyes-in-fluid, vanilla says not. Affects was_eye_in_water / is_under_water (swimming, overlay, air/drowning). The rest of the 26.3-form interaction (trackers, flow scaling, apply_to constants) is behaviourally equivalent for vanilla fluids - verified NOT divergences in the report. REPRODUCES 1.21.10 B1-G04.
items.title: Entity fluid interaction ships the 26.3 form; eye check uses camera height

items.evidence: Re-checked FIRST per the brief. Vanilla 1.21.11 FlowingFluid.canHoldAnyFluid bytecode read in full, fresh (FlowingFluid.txt:1012-1075): hardcoded list - LiquidBlockContainer -> true; blocksMotion -> false; excludes DoorBlock, #signs, ladder, sugar cane, bubble column, nether/end portals, end gateway, structure void; else true (air passes). Zero 'washed' references anywhere in FlowingFluid; washed_away_by_fluids is absent from 1.21.11 data (no tag file, no BlockTags field, no prepared key). The port's level/fluids.rs:359-361 ships the 26.3 tag form (is_liquid_container || in_set(washed_away_by_fluids)); Tags::resolve fills a missing tag with an EMPTY set, so can_hold_any_fluid is true only for liquid containers. Air does not hold fluid, so spread / spreadToSides / getNewLiquid find no valid target: NO fluid spreads at all, water or lava. The spread machinery itself matches vanilla exactly - the failure is isolated to the predicate. G5's status in the 1.21.7 ledger is 'fixed', but the 1.21.11 template carries the tag form - the fix never reached the template. REPRODUCES 1.21.10 B1-G05 and pilot G5.
items.title: NO fluid spreading at all, water or lava

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.11 LavaFluid.randomTick bytecode re-verified fresh: gates on ServerLevel.canSpreadFireAround(pos) (the radius rule), nextInt(3) passes, first branch cumulative offset(nextInt(3)-1, 1, nextInt(3)-1), isLoaded else return, air + hasFlammableNeighbours -> setBlockAndUpdate(BaseFireBlock.getState) + return, blocksMotion -> return (offset 115-123). The port's level/fluids.rs:776-785 stops only for the tag (tag('minecraft:blocks_lava_fire_spread').is_some_and(...)); BlockFacts::tag returns None for an absent tag, and blocks_lava_fire_spread does not exist in 1.21.11 data (no tag file, no BlockTags field, no prepared key) - so the walk never stops at a solid block: fire spreads through stone, and the walk keeps drawing RNG after the first motion-blocking block, perturbing the random stream vs vanilla. The rest of lava_random_tick (fluids.rs:747-808) matches vanilla exactly, including the radius-rule gate. REPRODUCES 1.21.10 B1-G06 and pilot G3.
items.title: Lava fire spread walks through solid blocks

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.11 FlowingFluid.getFlow's below-check reads BlockState.blocksMotion() (per-state rule; BlockBehaviour$BlockStateBase.blocksMotion verified in the jar). There is no blocks_fluid_flow tag in 1.21.11 data (no tag file, no BlockTags field, no prepared key). The port ships the 26.3 tag form in both places: horizon-client-render/src/assets.rs:224-232 (Assets::load reads minecraft:blocks_fluid_flow with .ok_or_else(|| invalid('missing fluid flow tag'))? - it would error even earlier on the equally absent blocks_motion_in_heightmap tag) and horizon-client/src/motion/fluids.rs:27-54 (FluidResources builds blocks_flow from assets.blocks_fluid_flow by block name instead of the per-state table). fluid_flow::flow_at consults blocks_fluid_flow for its below-check: with the tag absent, every neighbour reads as non-blocking, so flow vectors near solid blocks are computed as if the wall were not there - wrong push directions/magnitudes for entities, arrows, boats and mobs in water next to solids. Masking note: Assets::load is only called from render tests/examples, not the game's production startup path; the game's MotionResources::load fails on the missing #causes_suffocation / #suppresses_bounce tags (26.1 B3-G22 reproduces, Batch 3's scope). REPRODUCES 1.21.10 B1-G07.
items.title: Fluid-flow vector table reads the absent #blocks_fluid_flow tag

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.11 FallingBlockEntity.tick ends with deltaMovement.scale(0.98d) - the DOUBLE literal (ldc2_w // double 0.98d, offset 889, re-verified fresh). The port's horizon-client/src/entity_rules.rs:11-14 ships the 26.2 form: f64::from(0.98_f32) = 0.9800000190734863, not 0.98. Effect size: after 4 ticks, 0.1 x 0.98^4 = 0.092236816 vs 0.1 x 0.98F^4 = 0.09223682318... - a ~7e-9 relative drift per the 26.1 comment; over a 600-tick fall the accumulated relative difference is ~1.2e-5, sub-mm in position. Tiny but verified-wrong against the bytecode, and 26.1 had it right. scale_air_drag is shared with PrimedTnt.tick (out of scope). REPRODUCES 1.21.10 B1-G08.
items.title: Falling-block air drag uses 0.98F widened instead of the double literal 0.98

source: 1.21.11 parity sweep, batch 1 - the 1.21.7 pilot scope re-run against vanilla 1.21.11 (checks only, no fixes). Scope: water/lava spreading and flow, fluid pushing, bubble columns, concrete powder solidification, lava fire spread + ignition + game rules, dripstone growth + cauldron fill, falling blocks, cauldron fill levels, splash water. Re-checks all 21 items from the 1.21.10 run (PRIMARY: B1-G01..G11, B1-O01..O08, B11-G06, B11-G13) plus all six 1.21.7 pilot defects (G1-G6) and Batch 11 findings B11-G06, B11-G13 (SECONDARY), against 1.21.11's own jar/data.
systemic_note: The 1.21.7 pilot's systemic root cause (26.x tag-based logic for tags absent in the target version's data) applies to 1.21.11 in the same FIVE places as 1.21.10: the speleothem system (B1-G01) and splash water (B1-G03) as in 26.1, PLUS can_hold_any_fluid (B1-G05), the lava-fire walk (B1-G06), and the flow-vector table (B1-G07). A second regression is numeric: the falling-block air drag (B1-G08: 0.98F widened instead of the double literal). B1-G04 is the same pattern at a smaller scale (26.3-form entity fluid interaction, camera-height eye check). What is DIFFERENT about 1.21.11 is the direction of the remaining divergence. This tree is the TEMPLATE, so the five tag reads are the template's own unadapted residue, inherited down by the 1.21.10 child - but vanilla 1.21.11 itself MOVED TOWARD the template in three places, healing what were defects in 1.21.10: the environment-attribute system arrived (FAST_LAVA + INCREASED_FIRE_BURNOUT - the burnout gate B1-G09 is now correct, and the datapack-dimension fast_lava read is now the vanilla form), the game rules moved to the gamerules package with the radius rule replacing the doFireTick pair (the port's radius-form fire gate is now the vanilla form), and the vehicle.boat package arrived (healing one oracle break). The pattern is therefore not 'the tree ships 26.3 everywhere' but 'the tree ships 26.3 exactly where the port did not adapt - and vanilla has started adopting the 26.x forms the template already ships'. Where 1.21.11's data HAS the tag (#signs, #fire, #anvil, infiniburn, #soul_fire_base_blocks, #shovels, can_glide_through), the port reads it; where 1.21.11 still lacks the tag, the port usually carries the hardcoded 1.21.7-style list form - except in the five places above, where it ships the 26.3 form.
